name: commons-take-to-spend-v1
description: ⭐ DEAN'S VARIANT (09/09/2026), PUT TO THE ENGINE SESSION IN THESE WORDS: "You can play a card to a centre card to do the bonus action. OR, you can take all the cards from a central pile and then use those cards to pay for a bonus action of the matching type. So, if you take all the cards from the Draw card, they go into your hand. All the cards on the Harvest go into your barn. All the cards on the Build action can be spent to do a Build. All the cards on the Deliver action can immediately be used to deliver (this is one to watch, this could be crazy). All the cards on the Grow action are used to SOW (not grow, that would be crazy). Any cards that cannot be used are discarded. So, if there are 3 cards on the build action and you build a card that costs 1, the excess are discarded - they don't go into your hand." rules.turn.commonsTake: 'spend'. THE SHIPPED RULE IS 'harvest' (C5): a central pile is reached only through the Harvest action, whole pile into the harvester's BARN, and this overlay is paired against it - it sets no other knob, so every other rule in the game is exactly the shipped commons and the whole delta is this one flag. REUSES THE SAME commonsTake MOVE 'bonus' introduced (no fee, no card played), but the resolution now depends on WHICH BOARD is taken rather than always landing in the hand: orchard to HAND (as 'bonus'); wheat to BARN instead of hand, still no Harvest (D-S4, Harvest never reaches the centre under this knob either); dairy ONE card built from hand, paid FROM THE PILE ONLY (D-S1: no top-up from hand); vegetable ONE crate delivered to a tile with room, paid FROM THE PILE ONLY, the wild substitution applying within the pile (D-S1 again), scoring exactly as a barn delivery; apiary the WHOLE pile SOWN, one card at a time in pile order onto the taker's own non-full buildings, a card with no legal building discarded. Every card the chosen action does not use is DISCARDED to its own suit's pile (D-S2), never kept, never boxed - the first genuine discard sink this design has had since the two tolls left with the meeple economy. THE FOUR BUILDER DEFAULTS, none of them Dean's ruling: D-S1 a dairy/vegetable spend never tops up from hand or barn, pile only; D-S2 every unusable card is discarded, per its own suit; D-S3 a board is offered only if it can do something (the standing 'a door that can do nothing is not offered' ruling) - orchard/wheat whenever non-empty, dairy only if some hand card is payable from the pile, vegetable only if the pile can pay a crate for a tile with a free space, apiary only if the taker has a non-full building; D-S4 Harvest, main or bought, never reaches the centre under 'spend', exactly as under 'bonus'. ⭐ WHAT TO READ. a17-bonus-mix prints the SAME three columns 'bonus' introduced - PLAY (paid) / TAKE (free) / SLOT UNSPENT - read on the slot's TOTAL use, plus a 'takes by board' line that 'bonus' has no need of (every take there is the same shape; here the five boards do five different things). a18-commons-traffic's harvest-side readings - central harvests, the harvest histogram, the wheat-board split - all read 0 or 'no subject' BY CONSTRUCTION under this knob, for the same D-S4 reason 'bonus' states, and are replaced with takes per player per game BY BOARD, cards taken/used/discarded per game (the discard is the new sink), deliveries paid straight from the vegetable pile against every delivery in the game, the conservation line re-derived as plays = to hand + to barn + spent + discarded + stranded, and the farm-bypass reading moved to the WHEAT leg alone (a wheat take's barn gain against a seat's own buildings), beside Dean's 30-40% target. ⚠️ BOT BLINDNESS, named rather than fixed: the dairy/vegetable/apiary legs are priced through the normal built/delivered/cardPlaced events their task answers emit, but they reuse the plain build/deliver/sow TaskAnswer shapes, so handSpend and barnSpend cannot tell a pile-sourced payment from a hand- or barn-sourced one and overcharge it as if it were - the same admitted over-valuation this codebase already carries for a sow from hand against a sow from a deck top. The wheat leg alone is priced correctly (the harvest rate, off commonsTaken) because it has no task to hide behind. UNRUN BEFORE THIS PASS. ⛔ PASSENGERS PINNED 12/09/2026: Dean's plain-action balloon and Village Store ruling moved sixteen shipped leaves at once. This overlay predates that flip and every report taken against it does too, so each of those leaves is pinned here BY NAME at its PRE-FLIP value. Without it an arm read as a delta against a pre-flip base would silently gain a one-card flight, an always-present Aerodrome and a live coin economy. That is the 05/09/2026 passenger lesson: an overlay that should not move with the shipped default has to pin every knob the flip moved.
